name: Pharaoh-hophra and Egypt
charge: Saying, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself; a staff of reed to the house of Israel
summary: Judah leaned on Egypt against Babylon, and Egypt broke under the hand like a reed and ran into it. Ezekiel's word against Pharaoh is against the boast of ownership: the river was his, he had made it. Forty years of desolation were decreed, and Egypt was to be the basest of kingdoms afterward.
offense: The Lord addressed Pharaoh as the great dragon lying in the midst of his rivers, claiming the river as his own and saying that he had made it for himself. Egypt's strength had become a ground for boasting as though its provision came from Pharaoh's own power. Egypt had also been a staff of reed to the house of Israel. When they leaned upon it, it broke and injured them. The promised support encouraged a confidence it could not sustain. The remnant's later flight to Egypt repeated that misplaced reliance after the Lord had commanded them to remain in Judah.
judgment: Ezekiel announced Pharaoh's removal under the image of hooks in the dragon's jaws. The oracle pronounced desolation, scattering, and afterward a regathering in a lowly condition, so that Egypt would no longer be Israel's confidence. These are the terms of the prophetic sentence, including the forty years named in it. Jeremiah gave the remnant a particular sign: Pharaoh Hophra would be delivered to his enemies and those seeking his life, just as Zedekiah had been delivered to Nebuchadnezzar. The kingdom chosen as a refuge was itself under judgment; its ruler could not guarantee the safety he could not secure for himself.

entries.commentary: In the tenth year, tenth month, twelfth day, the word came to set Ezekiel's face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers and says, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself. The Most High will put hooks in his jaws, bring him up out of his rivers, and leave him thrown in the wilderness, because Egypt has been a staff of reed to the house of Israel that broke and tore their shoulder when they leaned upon it.

The Most High will bring a sword upon Egypt, cut off man and beast, and make the land utterly waste and desolate from Syene to the border of Ethiopia, uninhabited forty years, scattering the Egyptians among the nations. At the end of forty years He will bring the Egyptians again from where they were scattered into the land of Pathros, but they shall be a base kingdom, the basest of kingdoms, no more to rule over the nations or be the confidence of the house of Israel.

In the twenty-seventh year the word came that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon caused his army to serve a great service against Tyrus, yet had no wages for it, every head made bald and every shoulder peeled. Therefore the Most High gives the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar as wages for his army, because they wrought for Him; in that day the horn of the house of Israel will bud forth and Ezekiel will be given the opening of the mouth in their midst.

The word came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews dwelling in the land of Egypt and in the country of Pathros; the Most High reminded them of all the evil He had brought on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, now a desolation where no man dwelt, because of the wickedness they committed provoking Him to anger. They went to burn incense and serve other gods that neither they nor their fathers knew, yet the Most High sent all His servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, pleading with them not to do this abominable thing that He hates. The same work goes on today; we fill up the street corners all over the earth bringing forth the glorious gospel of the one true living God and Christ, the prophets He raised up to give warning. -

They hearkened not nor inclined their ear to turn from their wickedness and burn no incense to other gods, so the Most High's fury and anger was poured forth and kindled in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem until they were wasted and desolate. He asks why they commit this great evil against their own souls, cutting off man and woman, child and suckling out of Judah, leaving none to remain. They provoke Him to wrath with the works of their hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where they had gone to dwell, cutting themselves off to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth. -

The Most High asks whether they have forgotten the wickedness of their fathers, the kings of Judah, their wives, and their own wickedness committed in the land of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem; they were not humbled even to that day, nor did they fear or walk in His law and statutes. Therefore He will set His face against them for evil, to cut off all Judah, and take the remnant that set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there; they shall all be consumed and fall by the sword and the famine, from the least to the greatest. They shall become an execration, an astonishment, a curse, and a reproach; only a small number escaping the sword shall return, for none shall return to Judah though they have a desire to dwell there. -

All the men who knew their wives had burned incense to other gods, and all the women, a great multitude in Egypt and Pathros, answered Jeremiah defiantly. These men did not rule their houses well and had no authority over their households; their wives were in the midst of idolatry, the same disorder we see in this place spiritually called Egypt, in Babylon the great today. They said they would not hearken to the word spoken in the name of the Most High but would perform their vows to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings, claiming they had plenty of victuals and saw no evil until they left off, and then wanted all things and were consumed by the sword and famine. The women declared they made their cakes to worship her and poured out drink offerings without their men; the times women gather together without their men, such as baby showers with cakes and drinks and partying, are burning incense to other gods to keep in mind.

Jeremiah answered all the people, men and women, that the incense they burned in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, they and their fathers, kings, and princes, the Most High remembered and it came into His mind. The Most High could no longer bear the evil of their doings and the abominations they committed, therefore their land became a desolation, an astonishment, and a curse without an inhabitant as at that day. This evil happened to them because they burned incense and sinned against the Most High and did not obey His voice nor walk in His law, statutes, and testimonies.

Jeremiah told all the people and all the women that they and their wives had both spoken with their mouths and fulfilled with their hands their vows to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and would surely accomplish them. Therefore the Most High swore by His great name that His name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all Egypt, saying "The Lord GOD liveth"; He will watch over them for evil and not for good until they are consumed by the sword and famine. Only a small number escaping the sword shall return out of Egypt into Judah, and all the remnant that went to Egypt shall know whose words shall stand, His or theirs.

The Most High gives a sign that He will punish them in that place so they may know His words shall surely stand against them for evil; He will give Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies as He gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar. Evil does not come merely by chance; the Most High brings that evil upon us when we turn from Him and follow our own mind, sinning against the one true living God in Christ. -

The word of the Most High came to Jeremiah against the gentiles, against Egypt and the army of Pharaoh-necho king of Egypt by the river Euphrates at Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim. The Egyptians are gentiles and heathens; they are called to order the buckler and shield, draw near to battle, harness the horses, furnish the spears, and put on the brigandines. Yet the Most High has seen them dismayed and turned back, their mighty ones beaten down and fleeing without looking back, for fear was round about; the swift shall not flee away nor the mighty man escape, stumbling and falling toward the north by the river Euphrates.

Egypt rises up like a flood whose waters are moved like the rivers, boasting he will go up and cover the earth and destroy the city and its inhabitants, calling forth his horses, chariots, and mighty men, the Ethiopians, Libyans, and Lydians that handle the shield and bend the bow. But this is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance to avenge Him of His adversaries; the sword shall devour and be made drunk with their blood, for the Most High has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates. The virgin daughter of Egypt is told to go up into Gilead and take balm, but in vain shall she use many medicines, for she shall not be cured; the nations have heard of her shame and her cry filled the land as her mighty men stumbled and fell together.

The Most High spoke to Jeremiah how Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon should come and smite the land of Egypt; the word is to be declared in Migdol, Noph, and Tahpanhes, calling them to stand fast and prepare, for the sword shall devour round about them. Their valiant men are swept away and stand not because the Most High drove them; they fall one upon another and say let us go again to our own people and the land of our nativity from the oppressing sword. Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise who has passed the time appointed; as surely as Tabor is among the mountains and Carmel by the sea, so shall the conqueror come, and the daughter dwelling in Egypt must furnish herself to go into captivity, for Noph shall be waste and desolate without inhabitant.

Egypt is like a very fair heifer, but destruction comes out of the north; even her hired men in the midst of her are like fatted bullocks, turned back and fled away together, not standing because the day of their calamity and the time of their visitation was upon them. The voice shall go like a serpent as they march with an army and come against her with axes like hewers of wood to cut down her forest, though it cannot be searched, because they are more than the grasshoppers and are innumerable. The Most High will punish the multitude of No, Pharaoh, and Egypt with their gods and their kings, delivering them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar and his servants; afterward it shall be inhabited as in the days of old.

The Most High turns to comfort His own, telling Jacob His servant not to fear nor be dismayed, for He will save him from afar off and his seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease with none to make him afraid. He will make a full end of all the nations where He has driven us, but He will not make a full end of us; He will correct us in measure and will not leave us wholly unpunished, so there is redemption for us but still a reminder of punishment because of our sins.

Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help, staying on horses and trusting chariots, but not looking to the Holy One of Israel. This makes plain what chapter 30 opened with. We honor the Most High with our lips, but when the oppressor offers gifts we turn away and serve our oppressor's will. When Sennacherib's servant Rabshakeh offered Hezekiah two thousand horses, it was the same trick, a gift to pull the heart off the Most High. -

The Most High is also wise, will bring evil, and will not call back his words, but arises against the evildoers and against those who help them. The Egyptians are men and not God, their horses flesh and not spirit. When the Most High stretches out his hand, both the helper and the one helped fall down together. A nation cannot help you when the Most High has decided to punish both.

As a lion is not afraid of the shepherds' voices, so the Lord of hosts comes down to fight for Mount Zion, defending Jerusalem as birds flying. He will deliver, preserve, and pass over it. Therefore turn to him, from whom the children of Israel have deeply revolted; that revolt is the same rebellion of the rebellious children.

In that day every man casts away the idols of silver and gold his own hands made for a sin. Then the Assyrian falls by a sword that is not of man. He flees, his young men are discomfited, and his princes are afraid of the ensign, because the Most High's fire is in Zion and his furnace in Jerusalem. When the Most High brings his judgment, the heathen nations can do nothing, so we wait patiently while he waits for us to get ourselves together.

Ezekiel is to prophesy, Woe worth the day, for the day of the Lord is near, a cloudy day, the time of the heathen; the sword shall come upon Egypt and great pain in Ethiopia when the slain fall. Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, all the mingled people, and the men of the land that is in league shall fall with them by the sword; those that uphold Egypt shall fall and the pride of her power come down. -
Those "in league" are the peoples in agreement or alliance with Ethiopia, who fall together with Egypt by the sword.

The Most High will make the multitude of Egypt to cease by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and the terrible of the nations, who draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain, drying the rivers and selling the land into the hand of the wicked. He will destroy the idols, cause the images to cease out of Noph, set fire in Egypt, pour His fury upon Sin, cut off the multitude of No, and send the cities of Egypt into captivity, so they shall know that He is the Lord.

In the eleventh year the word came that the Most High has broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and it shall not be bound up to be healed or made strong to hold the sword. He will break both Pharaoh's arms, strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put His sword in his hand, scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and they shall know that He is the Lord. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry)

verses.text: In the tenth year, in the tenth month, in the twelfth day of the month, the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
Son of man, set thy face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him, and against all Egypt:

Speak, and say, Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I am against thee, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lieth in the midst of his rivers, which hath said, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself.

But I will put hooks in thy jaws, and I will cause the fish of thy rivers to stick unto thy scales, and I will bring thee up out of the midst of thy rivers, and all the fish of thy rivers shall stick unto thy scales.

And I will leave thee thrown into the wilderness, thee and all the fish of thy rivers: thou shalt fall upon the open fields; thou shalt not be brought together, nor gathered: I have given thee for meat to the beasts of the field and to the fowls of the heaven.
And all the inhabitants of Egypt shall know that I am the Lord, because they have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel.
When they took hold of thee by thy hand, thou didst break, and rend all their shoulder: and when they leaned upon thee, thou brakest, and madest all their loins to be at a stand.
Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I will bring a sword upon thee, and cut off man and beast out of thee.
And the land of Egypt shall be desolate and waste; and they shall know that I am the Lord: because he hath said, The river is mine, and I have made it.
Behold, therefore I am against thee, and against thy rivers, and I will make the land of Egypt utterly waste and desolate, from the tower of Syene even unto the border of Ethiopia.
No foot of man shall pass through it, nor foot of beast shall pass through it, neither shall it be inhabited forty years.

And I will make the land of Egypt desolate in the midst of the countries that are desolate, and her cities among the cities that are laid waste shall be desolate forty years: and I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and will disperse them through the countries.
Yet thus saith the Lord God; At the end of forty years will I gather the Egyptians from the people whither they were scattered:
And I will bring again the captivity of Egypt, and will cause them to return into the land of Pathros, into the land of their habitation; and they shall be there a base kingdom.
It shall be the basest of the kingdoms; neither shall it exalt itself any more above the nations: for I will diminish them, that they shall no more rule over the nations.
And it shall be no more the confidence of the house of Israel, which bringeth their iniquity to remembrance, when they shall look after them: but they shall know that I am the Lord God.

Thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will give Pharaoh–hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and that sought his life.
The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, saith; Behold, I will punish the multitude of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with their gods, and their kings; even Pharaoh, and all them that trust in him:

And I will deliver them into the hand of those that seek their lives, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants: and afterward it shall be inhabited, as in the days of old, saith the Lord.

Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the Lord!
Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words: but will arise against the house of the evildoers, and against the help of them that work iniquity.

Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the Lord shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together.
And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the first month, in the seventh day of the month, that the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and, lo, it shall not be bound up to be healed, to put a roller to bind it, to make it strong to hold the sword.
Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and will break his arms, the strong, and that which was broken; and I will cause the sword to fall out of his hand.
And I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and will disperse them through the countries.
And I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, and put my sword in his hand: but I will break Pharaoh’s arms, and he shall groan before him with the groanings of a deadly wounded man.

But I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, and the arms of Pharaoh shall fall down; and they shall know that I am the Lord, when I shall put my sword into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall stretch it out upon the land of Egypt.
And I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and disperse them among the countries; and they shall know that I am the Lord.
